newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks trend weaker in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks trend weaker in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks opened weaker on Friday morning as investors switched out of expensive looking blue chips in rotational buying of laggards, brokers said.
"We still see some upside for the index, although the market is likely to take a breather today," said Angus Shillington of institutional sales at Asia Equity.
The Hang Seng index was 49 points down at 11,965.87 after thirty minutes of trade on active volume of HK$1.11 billion.
The index had risen for seven straight session to 12,014.56 on Thursday, its first close above 12,000 since February 1994, but local stocks traded in London eased back overnight.
Most brokers, however, were not expecting a sizeable decline.
"Recent (U.S.) economic data are market-friendly, so we don't see alot of downside (in the Hang Seng) today," said one broker with a European house.

On Thursday, Washington reported factory orders had fallen 1.9 percent in August, the steepest drop since January 1993, keeping a cap on inflation fears. Some investors are also awaiting U.S. employment data due later on Friday, brokers said.
"The big movers yesterday were laggards and that is likely to be the main theme today," said Asia Equity's Shillington.
Mid-cap and China-incorporated H shares were among the favoured laggards.
Among the H shares, Shanghai Petrochemical rose HK$0.02 to HK$2.10, while Yizhen advanced HK$0.03 to HK$1.91.
Qingling Motors lead the sector, putting on HK$0.20 to HK$3.20. The company was one of only two H share companies to report earnings growth in the first six months of 1996.
In the mid-cap sector, Giordano Internnational gained HK$0.40 to HK$7.50 on hopes of improving business prospects in China.
Most blue chips came in for profit-taking on Friday morning, with the utilities sector leading the market down.
China Light dropped HK$0.10 to HK$35.70 and Hong Kong Telecom lost HK$0.15 to HK$14.25.

In the finance sector, Hang Seng Bank bucked the downtrend putting on HK$0.25 to HK$84.00, matching its all time high. HSBC, which survived profit-taking overnight in London, dropped HK$0.50 to HK$145.00.

Among the properties, Sun Hung Kai Properties looked the strongest adding HK$1.00 to HK$82.50, after briefly touching HK$82.75. The share had drifted down on Thursday after reporting mediocre results for 1996 on Wednesday.
